title: Cross-functional playbook for launching a new model into the catalog (coordination & release)
creator: Riley Ortega
description:
Context:
We are adding a new model variant to the public model catalog. This ticket is the PM-facing, cross-functional playbook to coordinate benchmarks, runtime compatibility, doc artifacts, release notes, console metadata, and the public announcement. The goal is to have a repeatable checklist that any PM can run for future model additions with clear owners, deadlines, and rollback criteria.

Scope (what this ticket coordinates):
- Performance & cost profile: latency percentiles, throughput, recommended batch configs, quantization notes.
- Compatibility checks: API surface parity, streaming behavior, function-calling support, tokenization differences.
- Console & catalog metadata: model card, tags, capabilities, example prompts, safety labels.
- Docs & examples: quickstart snippets, SDK examples, migration notes for breaking changes.
- Benchmarks & verification: internal perf tests, eval scorecard, regression alert baselines.
- Release notes & external comms: coordinated PR, changelog entry, blog/announcement plan, social blurbs.
- Launch runbook: canary rollout plan, metric watchlist, rollback triggers, support escalation path.
- Legal/security: privacy classification, KMS/HSM implications, export controls, and completed security review.

High-level timeline (milestones):
- Week -3: Performance profiling and end-to-end compatibility tests completed by ENG. Documentation skeleton prepared by Docs.
- Week -2: Internal sign-off on benchmarks, console metadata drafted, release notes initial draft.
- Week -1: Final security review and legal sign-off, marketing assets ready, support training completed.
- Launch day: Publish catalog entry, push release notes, route traffic through canary targets.
- +72h: Post-launch assessment and decide on full rollout or rollback.

Checklist (action items with suggested owners):
1) Performance & runtime (owner: ENG-Perf lead - Devon Chen)
   - Run 99/95/50 latency & p50/p95 token cost benchmark vs baseline models (ENG-4127).
   - Validate continuous batching and KV cache behavior under representative request mixes.
   - Produce "recommended runtime profile" for console (batch sizes, concurrency, quantization profile).

2) API & SDK compatibility (owner: SDK lead - Priya Singh)
   - Confirm streaming endpoints and function-calling semantics match Redwood API expectations.
   - Add SDK examples for Python/Node showing generation, chat, and embeddings if supported.

3) Benchmarks & quality (owner: Applied ML - Tomas Nguyen)
   - Run eval suite (summarization, instruction-following, safety prompts) and attach scorecard.
   - Define regression thresholds and required alerts in Redwood Optimize.

4) Docs & examples (owner: Docs - Lina Kor)
   - Write model card: intended use cases, limitations, prompt examples, pricing notes.
   - Create migration guide if tokenizer or output shape differs.
   - Ensure docs hosted and tested in staging docs site.

5) Console & catalog entry (owner: Console PM - Maya Patel)
   - Populate catalog metadata: tags, capabilities, sample prompts, cost-estimates.
   - Add model to performance dashboards and per-model tracing hooks.

6) Release notes & comms (owner: Marketing - Omar Reyes)
   - Draft public release notes with TL;DR, key benchmarks, and migration guidance.
   - Prepare blog post outline, social copy, and example customer-facing email.

7) Support & SRE readiness (owner: Support Lead - Keisha Brown / SRE - Aaron Li)
   - Create internal playbook for common issues and FAQ.
   - Set up dedicated monitor dashboard and alerting with on-call run sequence.

8) Legal & Security (owner: Security - Helena Park)
   - Complete privacy & export control review and update model card.
   - Confirm KMS/HSM usage and document data flow for private deployments.

9) Rollout plan (owner: PM)
   - Canary: route ~5% traffic to new model for 24-72 hours with automatic health checks.
   - Metrics to monitor: user-facing latency p95, error rate, token cost variance, eval score drift, customer support tickets.
   - Rollback criteria: sustained >15% latency regression, >3x baseline error rate, or major quality regression on key evals.

Communications matrix (who to notify and when):
- Pre-launch (48h): ENG, Docs, Console, Support, Security, Marketing, Sales ops.
- Launch (T0): Internal #launches channel, release PR, update docs link.
- Post-launch (+24h): Metric snapshot and decision to expand traffic.

Artifacts & links (placeholders to be filled):
- Performance dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/models/PM-8672
- Perf runbook & artifacts: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MC/PM-8672+perf
- Draft release notes PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/xxxx
- Docs staging: https://docs-staging.redwood.ai/models/orion-xl
- Support playbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/pm-8672-support

Open questions / trade-offs noted:
- Should we enable default quantized variants in the catalog or surface as "advanced" option? (trade-off: cost vs perceived quality).
- Migration path for customers with custom tokenizers — do we provide conversion tools or recommend re-tokenization?
- If security review identifies export-control risk, what is the expected cadence for mitigation?

Follow-ups after launch:
- 72h post-launch retrospective with Eng/Docs/SRE/Support to capture issues and action items.
- Update Optimize rules with any new batching suggestions observed in production.
- Add a permanent dashboard tile for this model's unit economics in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Performance profiles published and verified in staging with p50/p95/p99 numbers
Model card and docs published with examples and migration notes
Release notes drafted and approved by Marketing and Legal
Security review completed and any required mitigations tracked
Canary rollout executed and post-launch metrics within defined thresholds
Support playbook available and support team trained

rollout_plan: Canary at 5% for 24-72h → expand to 25% if stable → full rollout after 7 days of stable metrics. Automatic rollback on defined thresholds. Staged customers (enterprise tenants) to be contacted 48h before full migration.

support ticket volume for the new model
